values: OWR-4132-003 (30001370): Common basin boundaries in the bistable mean-field interval map

Common L1 basin boundaries for a bistable mean-field interval map — Alec Kriebel (ORCID0009-0001-9320-500X), v1.0. Preprint date: 2026-10-03. Resolves the stated common L1 basin-boundary conjecture for the prescribed two-branch Mobius model with feedback A tanh(Bm/A), A in (0,2/5], B in (6,16]. The central basin equals both stable basin boundaries in the relative L1 topology of every probability density, and equals the closure of finite preimages of the constant density. Unbounded densities and zeros are included. Global convergence, the analytic-core boundary seed, invariant representations and the inverse-expansion method are credited to Bardet, Keller and Zweimuller; the new full-density backward transport and open-map argument complete the extension. Dated bounded primary-literature audit found no equivalent earlier theorem in inspected material; the final foundational journal proof version, unpublished work and incomplete indexing remain coverage limits. No global novelty certification. Six-page unrefereed preprint; extensive AI use and no independent external human peer review. Two sequential fresh full adversarial review rounds completed with every mandatory finding resolved. PDF plus portable source/verification ZIP preserves37 original problem artifacts and includes exact contraction/distortion certificates, rough-density controls and the bounded priority dossier. Primary question: https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46250, Keller printed2715/PDF17. Record: https://zenodo.org/records/23129302. Reviewed PR: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/359.

records.title: Common L1 basin boundaries for a bistable mean-field interval map
records.description: We prove the common-basin-boundary conjecture stated by Keller in the 2009 Oberwolfach mini-workshop on the spectrum of transfer operators. For the prescribed two-branch Mobius interval maps with feedback G(m)=A tanh(Bm/A), A in (0,2/5] and B in (6,16], the basin of the constant density equals the boundary of each noncentral stable basin in the relative L1 topology of all probability densities. The central basin is also exactly the L1 closure of the finite preimages of the constant density. A terminal cumulative transport is lifted backward with self-consistent feedback; a probability-space inverse contraction and uniform distortion bound cover arbitrary integrable densities, including unbounded densities and densities with zeros. The global three-limit theorem, boundary seed, invariant integral representations and inverse-expansion mechanism are credited to Bardet, Keller and Zweimuller. A self-contained research note and portable verification supplement accompany the result. A dated bounded primary-literature audit found no earlier equivalent theorem; it does not certify global novelty, and the final journal proof version of the foundational paper was not obtained. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received independent external human peer review.
